messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired: synthetic-check-sa-01 — 87% probes 5xx over 3m (fired at 02:21 UTC). Link: https://pd.company/INC12345
Maya (oncall): acked on PagerDuty. I'm looking. Any idea if this is prober or backend? :eyes:
PagerDuty: ACK by Maya (oncall) at 02:22 UTC
Raj: seeing a fanout spike from the prober cluster to sa-modelpool. lots of 502/504 from the model gateway around 02:19-02:23. CPU on the gateway nodes is fine but connection backlog is climbing.
Kelsey: pulled prober logs — we have a burst of concurrent probes (concurrency=200) against the SA endpoint after a scheduled sweep. Prober retries are aggressive. here's the snippet from the prober config that changed in last deploy:
```
probe_concurrency: 200
retry_policy:
  attempts: 4
  backoff_ms: 100
```
Tom (support): Got a few customer reports about slow responses for embeddings in SA region (~2% of requests with >1s tail). Not widespread but correlated timeframe.
Maya (oncall): initial customer impact: small but visible latency tail. No full outages. We'll treat as SEV-2 until contained.
Raj: digging into model gateway logs — many upstream connections reset with EPIPE. Looks like the gateway's keepalive pools exhausted. Might be too many short lived connections from the prober.
Kelsey: temporary mitigation: can we throttle the prober fanout and add a short jitter? I can push a config change to prober manager if we want.
Maya (oncall): do it. Also scaling the gateway pool up by 2 nodes to buy breathing room. Raj, can you trigger? I'll coordinate PD suppression for noisy repeats.
Raj: scaling gateway pool now (autoscale API):
```
POST /infra/api/v1/scale
{"service":"model-gateway-sa","replicas":+2}
```
Raj: scale API returned 202, new nodes provisioning.
PagerDuty: PagerDuty note: suppression rule applied for synthetic-check-sa-01 to avoid repeated flapping pages while mitigation in flight.
Kelsey: pushed prober config with reduced concurrency and added jitter:
```
probe_concurrency: 30
retry_policy:
  attempts: 2
  backoff_ms: 250
jitter_ms: 100-500
```
Kelsey: restarted prober manager. Rolling changes across 4 regions (sa prober pool) complete at 02:30 UTC.
Maya (oncall): observed dropped probe rate and fewer upstream errors. Good so far.
Tom (support): Customers seeing latency returning to normal in the affected samples. I'll update the support thread: "Investigating synthetic probes caused short-lived latency spike in SA region; service impact limited; mitigations applied." Will attach CI graphs.
Raj: gateway nodes came up at 02:34 UTC; connection backlog decreased and 5xx rate dropped to baseline by ~02:36.
Maya (oncall): handing off to Raj for post-incident follow-up and RCA. I'll remain available for support comms.
Raj: taking postmortem. Initial hypothesis: recent prober sweep increased concurrency beyond what the model gateway's connection pooling expected, exhausting transient connection capacity and triggering cascading 5xx. Action items:
- INF-711: Add circuit-breaker on prober -> gateway to cap concurrency (Kelsey)
- INF-712: Harden gateway keepalive and connection pooling defaults (Raj)
- INF-713: Add rate-limited probe rollout in scheduler to avoid simultaneous sweeps (Maya)
- INF-714: Update support playbook and customer messaging template (Tom)
Charlie (eng-lead): thanks team. Please include exact timestamps, config git SHAs, and the prober deploy that introduced the concurrency bump in the postmortem. Also schedule a follow-up sync with infra and devex next week. :thumbsup:
Maya (oncall): creating incident ticket INC12345 and linking to INF tasks. Will attach metrics and logs. Final status: mitigated, no ongoing customer outage. Will mark this as SEV-2 and move to RCA phase.
incident-bot: Incident INC12345 created: https://issues.company/INC12345 — assigned to Raj. Severity: SEV-2 — status: mitigated
Maya (oncall): closing the paging loop. If anything regresses ping me. Good job everyone. :tada:
